title: The window and the canopy: the issue window, you at the cleaning table, the rifle stripped on the mat and the weapon card's dirt
about: v0.0.28, "The window and the canopy", draws your R-7 at the armoury's issue window, takes it to the 25 m lane and back, and cleans it under the canopy before the armourer's inspection. Four looks are new and scored first; every picture is the game's own code where the game has it (the people composed and shaded by the figure engine at the stage's 16 px a metre in utilities, snapped to the Mars palette; the stage's camera from 45 degrees above; the stage's own 16 px R-7; the weapon card painted by the game's card), and the candidate's piece is the sample's alone, so the game is unchanged until you score. W, the window: a strip of the armoury's south face with window 1 in it (1.2 m wide, its counter 1.1 m high and 0.6 m deep), the armourer behind it, the rifle across the counter with its bolt open, and you at the customer spot beside it, three times larger and at its own size: W-a (the default) the counter at the hip and the upper half open, W-b a grille over the upper half. F, you at the cleaning table (2.4 by 0.9 m, 0.9 m high) at its north spot facing the camera, the mat before you, in daylight and under the canopy's evening lamps: F-a (the default) the lean the sink already uses, no new frame; F-b a pair of its own, a hand on a part over the mat and the cleaning rod held up to the light, two new frames. By depth the stage would draw you behind the table's top, which hides you below 0.6 m; your hands are drawn over it where they reach it. M, the mat (1.0 by 0.4 m, 16 by 6 pixels on the stage) in its five frames by the clean's part (the rifle whole, laid out dirty with grit on the upper and carbon at the bolt, cleaned, oiled, together again) and the air hose's puff: M-a (the default) the Corps' olive rubber, M-b a tan canvas roll-out, more contrast for the black parts. D, the weapon card at each word the game uses for a rifle's state (fine, gritty, fouled, wants cleaning): D-a (the default) dust as tan speckle on the receiver's upper edges and in the open port, carbon at the port and the muzzle, heavier at wants cleaning, fine as today; D-b the card as today, the word only. Not sampled, built at these and yours to ask about: the clearing barrel (a sand drum, its tube at 45 degrees), the tables, the solvent tanks and the air hoses, the rank's rings on the apron, the second window. The game builds the defaults until you score.
